security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, the SRET/MRET/MNRET event modules unconditionally clear mstatus.MDT, mstatus.SDT, and vsstatus.SDT during return-from-trap execution without any extension-enable gate. Specifically: SretEvent.scala:106 unconditionally writes MDT=0 during SRET-in-M (no hasSmdbltrp check); SretEvent.scala:108-109 unconditionally writes SDT=0 on SRET-in-HS and SRET-in-M-to-U/VS/VU (no hasSsdbltrp/DTE check); MretEvent.scala:72 unconditionally writes MDT=0 on every MRET; MretEvent.scala:74 writes SDT=0 when returning to non-M/non-HS (no Ssdbltrp gate); MNretEvent.scala:76-78 same pattern with no Smdbltrp/Ssdbltrp qualifier. The CSR module defines mdtInit=0 (NewCSR.scala:71) violating spec MDT reset=1. No hasSmdbltrp or hasSsdbltrp configuration signal exists anywhere in the NewCSR subtree to gate these side effects, meaning the hardware performs these bit manipulations regardless of whether the extensions are actually implemented in the core configuration.
security_spec.summary: SRET/MRET/MNRET unconditionally clear MDT and SDT in mstatus/vsstatus without checking Smdbltrp/Ssdbltrp extension enable, corrupting reserved CSR bits when extensions are absent
